approachQuestion.prompt:
Index-grid checksum. A conceptual grid has n rows and m columns. Cell (i,j) has value i+j for zero-based indices 0<=i<n and 0<=j<m. Return the sum of all cell values. The input consists only of n and m, not a stored grid. There are 1 <= n,m <= 10,000. The result and every intermediate expression in the listed methods fit signed 64-bit. Addition, multiplication, comparison, and exact integer division on these words cost constant time. Choose minimum worst-case time, then peak auxiliary space. Return one integer; do not output grid cells.

Example 1: Input: n=2,m=3. Output: 9; rows are [0,1,2] and [1,2,3].
Example 2: Input: n=1,m=1. Output: 0.

options.text: Return m times n*(n-1)/2 plus n times m*(m-1)/2, evaluating each product before its exact division by two.
options.feedback: Each row index appears in m cells and each column index in n cells. Their arithmetic-series totals can be combined without visiting individual cells.

options.text: Sum indices 0..n-1 in one loop and 0..m-1 in another, then return m times the first sum plus n times the second.
options.feedback: This recognizes the separate row and column contributions and is correct, but each index sum can be evaluated directly from the given dimension.

options.text: Use nested row and column loops, adding i+j to a total for each cell.
options.feedback: The total is correct, but the entire grid is defined by two dimensions and a fixed formula. Cell-by-cell traversal repeats work that the factored arithmetic avoids.

options.text: Return n*m*(n+m-2), the cell count times the largest cell value.
options.feedback: Not all cells have the maximum value. For n=2,m=3, this returns 18 rather than the required 9.

feedback.reason: A scalar aggregate of a formula-defined grid can be computed without enumerating its conceptual cells.
details: Compute rowSum=n*(n-1)/2 and columnSum=m*(m-1)/2 using the guaranteed exact word arithmetic. Return m*rowSum+n*columnSum. Do not allocate a grid, generate cell values, or loop over indices.

For a 2-by-3 grid, row indices contribute 3*(0+1)=3 and column indices contribute 2*(0+1+2)=6, totaling 9. The input is only two dimensions and the output one integer, so no explicit grid cells need to be generated. Exact word arithmetic makes the two series formulas valid without a traversal.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze factor-index-sums for independent dimensions n and m under the stated fixed-size word-operation model. What are worst-case time and peak auxiliary space? There is no supplied grid to read and the required output is one integer.
constraints: Choose the tightest standard bound for the complete execution. Count peak simultaneously live auxiliary storage; exclude supplied input and required output.
Word arithmetic, indexing, and copying one fixed-size element take constant time. No hashing or recursion is used.

options.text: O(n + m) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Two arithmetic-series formulas and fixed scalar operations give constant time and space.
details: The formula uses a fixed number of word additions, multiplications and exact divisions regardless of n or m. Its intermediate values fit the declared word model, so both time and auxiliary space are O(1). The conceptual grid is neither input storage nor required output, and is never materialized. This does not claim constant bit-complexity for arbitrary-precision integers.
“O(n + m) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: That describes explicitly summing row and column indices, whereas the analyzed method uses arithmetic-series formulas.
“O(nm) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: That describes enumerating cells; the formula avoids all such visits.
“O(nm) time, O(nm) auxiliary space”: No grid is constructed, copied, or returned, so neither area-sized work nor area-sized storage belongs to this method.
